Judgment
1.

Vide this order, I propose to dispose off these two criminal revision petitions filed against the impugned order dated 06.04.2019 passed by the Ld. CMM, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi,
whereby accused persons have been discharged.

2. The genesis of any criminal action lies in the complaint made by the complainant describing the facts and events so that the investigating agency and the Court can come to a conclusion or form an opinion as to the commission of an offence.
Kulbhushan Tyagi vs . State And Ors.

3. Upfront, a reference made by made to the complaint made by the complainant in the present case:
Respected Sir, I have booked a Commercial Plot of size 120 Sq. yards in Jaipuria Greens, NH-24, Bamhetta, Ghaziabad Project.
I have deposited an amount of Rs.7,05,000/- (Rs. Seven Lakh and Five Thousand only) according to company payment plan.
Then company declared that they will provide me a commercial plot in next nine months.

But unfortunately company did not provide me commercial plot till dated 26/05/2007 then after many visits to the company office, I was never given a satisfactory reply nor was I ever able to meet the owner of the company.

Because that time I was very needy of my money, so I decided to get refund my money with interest (as per as company norms in application form) but after a hard struggle I got only Rs.7,05,000/-
(Rs. Seven Lakh and Five Thousand only) and company denied to pay the interest.

Doubtfully when I checked the DETAIL PROJECT REPORT of this project in Ghaziabad Development Authority (G.D.A) I was shocked to know that company doesn't has the actual land against which they have taken the money.
When I contacted Ghaziabad Development Authority (G.D.A) they declared that never given a permission to take a booking amount without acquiring the whole land for this project.
Right Now I am very helpless and because this is the case of fraud and cheating with me by above company and its directors.
So I request yourself to kindly interfere and take a proper action against this company & Its directors.
I will be so thankful to you.

Dated 19/01/2010 Applicant KULABHUSHAN TYAGI 94-A DUNDAHERA, NEAR ABES ENGG.
COLLEGE, VIJAY NAGAR BY PASS ROAD, GHAZIABAD-201009 MOB.
4. In the first complaint, the grievance seems to be only pertaining to interest amount.
A similar complaint was made viz-a-viz a residential plot booked by the complainant.
In the second complaint, the complainant is aggrieved by the fact that the plot assured was not given.
5. Although after detailed investigation, a charge- sheet was filed in the present case.
I am constrained to note that the complaint is not disclosing complete facts or at least is not presenting the facts accurately.
The version of the complainant is distorted and contrary to record, i.e. that material placed on record by the IO, most of which has been collected from the complainant himself.
6. I would, therefore, first refer to the initial agreement made between the parties.

are contrary to the facts as emerging from the Advance Registration Form.
9. As per the charge-sheet, such an offer was made on 20.06.2007 whereby a provisional allotment of Plot No. H-74, Block-H was made to the complainant Kulbhushan Tyagi.
Other persons were also offered provisional allotment around the same date.
This is clearly 16 months after the advance payment was made by the complainant to the accused.
10. In these circumstances, the following conclusions can be arrived at on the mere reading of the documents.

Firstly, the Advance Registration Form dated 16.02.2006 made no specific promise or gave no specific assurance that the complainant would be entitled to a plot in any particular group housing scheme and definitely not in project "Sunrise Green".
Secondly, the agreement was more of the nature of a deposit made with the accused company with the assurance that in case no project was launched or even if a project was launched but no allotment was made within six months, for the period beyond that complainant would be entitled to interest.
There was a further clause that if by any chance no allotment was made within nine months, the complainant would be entitled to seek refund alongwith interest.

11. Therefore, clearly the breach as contemplated in clause (d) of the Advance Registration Form stood committed at the end of the period of nine months or in the other words the contingency had arisen which entitled the complainant to cancel the contract and seek refund.
What did the complainant do?

The complainant ignored the breach, failed to rescind the contract and waived any right to claim either rescission or damages by sitting quietly till the provisional allotment was made 16 months after the date of Advance Registration Form and more specifically for a period of 07 months after the contingency had arisen such a waiver continued by the conduct of the complainant.
12. This conduct shows that even the complainant understood or treated that time was not the essence of contract in the present case.

In any event, the right to seek refund guaranteed under the contract was never enforced and I do not find any further allegation that the complainant enforced his right to seek specific performance of the contract.
13. In any event, the allotment letter which was so prepared on 20.06.2007 also indicated that the allotment was provisional.

All throughout the complainant continued to not exercise his right to seek cancellation of the contract for allotment of residential plot on account of delay on part of the accused, which contingency was contemplated from the very beginning in the advance registration form.
The balance 72.50% of the amount was not paid in terms of Advance Registration Form.
The reciprocal promises were therefore not performed.

The matter does not ends here.

Of course, the accused offered an allotment of a plot by way of provisional letter dated 20.06.2007 but the contents of the same also indicate that this allotment did not also guarantee actual handing over of the plot.
Needless to say that by this stage, the entire amount payable for a 200 Sq. yard property was not paid by the complainant.
The complainant had only made the initial advance payment and the remaining payment was to be made based on the stage of development of project.
15. At this juncture, it may be relevant to refer to some of the provisions of the Indian Contract Act.

55. Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract in which time is essential.--When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract.

Effect of such failure when time is not essential.--If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at or before the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure.

Effect of acceptance of performance at time other than that agreed upon.--If, in case of a contract voidable on account of the promisors failure to perform his promise at the time agreed, the promisee accepts performance of such promise at any time other than that agreed, the promisee cannot claim compensation for any loss occasioned by the non- performance of the promise at the time agreed, unless,at the time of such acceptance, he gives notice to the promisor of his intention to do so.
63.Promise may dispense with or remit performance of promisee.--Every promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, the performance of the promisee made to him, or may extend the time for such performance,or may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit.
16.
It seems that both the parties have till date not rescinded or terminated the contract.
No civil proceedings were ever initiated by the complainant alleging that there was a breach of contract or that the complainant was entitled to any damages.
The Arbitration clause also has not been invoked.

Clearly, in law the same amounts to waiver of right or acquiescence in the breach and in the alternative, the same can be taken to indicate that the complainant wishes to wait for the allotment of plot and did not intend to exercise his right guaranteed under the agreement to seek refund.

It is a separate matter that as far as case of Kulbhushan Tyagi is concerned, he has already obtained refund of the amount of the commercial plot and is claiming that he is entitled to the residential plot under the scheme.
17. In my view, since neither party had terminated the contract despite the obvious breach or delay or the contingency having occurred, it seems that time was never essence of the present contract.
The contract is still subsisting and in terms of the contract the right of the complainant to seek refund or interest has not been invoked by the complainant till date.
The terms and conditions of the various documents executed between the parties are at variance with the contents of the complaint.

8 18.
Unfortunately, when the parties sign an agreement they become bound by the terms.

In the present case, the complainant signed the initial deposit agreement (Advance Registration Form)
with open eyes and now cannot claim that he had entered into a contract for allotment of a specific plot in the project Sunrise Greens.
The complainant has conveniently in the complaint tried to present a different story than from the actual contract entered into between the parties as decipherable from the said document.
From the bare reading, it can be said that there was no dishonest intention on part of the accused while seeking the payment of money from the complainant.
There was no project indicated in the document which clearly suggested that if a project was launched in the future the company may allot a plot to the complainant.
Once the complainant agreed to such a vague contract, he is equally bound by the terms and cannot claim otherwise.

The booking amount was not taken against any particular contract and the argument that before the land was alloted to the accused, the accused could not have made any allotment of land or booked for sale any property in the project falls on its face as clearly the amount was not paid nor sought against the project "Sunrise Greens" at any stage and the complainant is well aware of this position.
19.

In these circumstances, also considering that project is still underway and as per the record i.e.
the documents available with the chargesheet, the accused had informed the IO that it had executed 352 sale deeds and remaining purchasers had taken refund of the advance amount, which claim is not disputed in the chargesheet by the IO.
The order on discharge cannot be disturbed.
Breach of contract cannot be converted into a criminal offence of cheating.

It is settled law that it has to be shown that the intention of the accused was either dishonest from the very beginning or it must be specifically shown as to at which stage the intention became dishonest.

20. Needless to say there is one more aspect which needs to be highlighted at this stage i.e. that under the agreement with the Ghaziabad Development Authority (GDA) while the builder i.e. the accused was suppose to purchase or procure some percentage of land, the remaining was to be provided by the GDA which failed to make such land available.
21. Chargesheet records the claim of the accused:
Based on the above licence, a Detailed Project Report (DPR) was presented for development of a housing scheme conceived on 300 Acres of land.
Out of which 180 acres were to be owned by the company and the remaining 120 Acres were to be contributed by GDA after acquiring the same.
It was thus being essence of proposal later on approved and terms were reduced in writing in the form of Developers Agreement 13.02.2007 with the Ghaziabad Development Authority (GDA).

However, the GDA without any justification initially deferred their part of performance under agreement dated 13.02.07 for some time and later on backtrack completely, leaving only 180 Acres of land necessitating drastic revision.
Under these compelling circumstances beyond its control in lieu of the layout plan filed alongwith DPR on 18.11.2006, a revised plan was prepared and submitted on 07.12.2010 to GDA for approval.

The revised plan approval for the project was finally got approved by SMV Agencies Pvt. Ltd. vide letter No.389/M.P./2010 dated 07.12.2010, which Kulbhushan Tyagi vs . State And Ors. on 17 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136363402/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, in case the company was not in a position to make any offer for allotment within a period of nine months, the complainant had a right to withdraw a money and asked for refund by giving 30 days notice.
This is clearly 16 months after the advance payment was made by the complainant to the accused.
Firstly, the Advance Registration Form dated 16.02.2006 made no specific promise or gave no specific assurance that the complainant would be entitled to a plot in any particular group housing scheme and definitely not in project "Sunrise Green".
Secondly, the agreement was more of the nature of a deposit made with the accused company with the assurance that in case no project was launched or even if a project was launched but no allotment was made within six months, for the period beyond that complainant would be entitled to interest.
There was a further clause that if by any chance no allotment was made within nine months, the complainant would be entitled to seek refund alongwith interest.
11. Therefore, clearly the breach as contemplated in clause (d) of the Advance Registration Form stood committed at the end of the period of nine months or in the other words the contingency had arisen which entitled the complainant to cancel the contract and seek refund.
The complainant ignored the breach, failed to rescind the contract and waived any right to claim either rescission or damages by sitting quietly till the provisional allotment was made 16 months after the date of Advance Registration Form and more specifically for a period of 07 months after the contingency had arisen such a waiver continued by the conduct of the complainant.
12. This conduct shows that even the complainant understood or treated that time was not the essence of contract in the present case.
All throughout the complainant continued to not exercise his right to seek cancellation of the contract for allotment of residential plot on account of delay on part of the accused, which contingency was contemplated from the very beginning in the advance registration form.
Unfortunately, when the parties sign an agreement they become bound by the terms.
In the present case, the complainant signed the initial deposit agreement (Advance Registration Form)
with open eyes and now cannot claim that he had entered into a contract for allotment of a specific plot in the project Sunrise Greens.
The complainant has conveniently in the complaint tried to present a different story than from the actual contract entered into between the parties as decipherable from the said document.
From the bare reading, it can be said that there was no dishonest intention on part of the accused while seeking the payment of money from the complainant.
There was no project indicated in the document which clearly suggested that if a project was launched in the future the company may allot a plot to the complainant.
Once the complainant agreed to such a vague contract, he is equally bound by the terms and cannot claim otherwise.
The booking amount was not taken against any particular contract and the argument that before the land was alloted to the accused, the accused could not have made any allotment of land or booked for sale any property in the project falls on its face as clearly the amount was not paid nor sought against the project "Sunrise Greens" at any stage and the complainant is well aware of this position.
19.
In these circumstances, also considering that project is still underway and as per the record i.e.
the documents available with the chargesheet, the accused had informed the IO that it had executed 352 sale deeds and remaining purchasers had taken refund of the advance amount, which claim is not disputed in the chargesheet by the IO.
Breach of contract cannot be converted into a criminal offence of cheating.
It is settled law that it has to be shown that the intention of the accused was either dishonest from the very beginning or it must be specifically shown as to at which stage the intention became dishonest.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The order on discharge cannot be disturbed.
Based on the above licence, a Detailed Project Report (DPR) was presented for development of a housing scheme conceived on 300 Acres of land.
Out of which 180 acres were to be owned by the company and the remaining 120 Acres were to be contributed by GDA after acquiring the same.
It was thus being essence of proposal later on approved and terms were reduced in writing in the form of Developers Agreement 13.02.2007 with the Ghaziabad Development Authority (GDA).
However, the GDA without any justification initially deferred their part of performance under agreement dated 13.02.07 for some time and later on backtrack completely, leaving only 180 Acres of land necessitating drastic revision.
Under these compelling circumstances beyond its control in lieu of the layout plan filed alongwith DPR on 18.11.2006, a revised plan was prepared and submitted on 07.12.2010 to GDA for approval.
1)That the company has got the layout plans approved as per the details given below:
a. DPR Approval : 116/Niyojan / 06 dated 29.11.2016, 300 Acre.
Village road to be superimposed on plan 3. Compulsion to imbibe the encroached land in drawing 4.
Overall area reduced by 10%
5. Incorporate temples, cremation ground in the drawing.
6. Incorporation of gas pipeline to create a green corridor of 18 M. b. 29.11.2010 to 12.02.2014 Reason for layout change:
1. Purchase of more land 2. Unavailability of land of entry to H block 3. Change in the location of EWS and LIG due to land dispute.
4. Increase of F.A.R. From 1.5 to 2.5.
5. Provisioning of extra services area for the customers.
3) It is thus clear that the total project area got reduced from 300 acre in 2006 to 279.415 acre in 2014 necessitating the plot area to be reduced by 10% besides other unforeseen reasons.
Kulbhushan Tyagi vs . State And Ors.
Therefore, if the land pool fall short due to supervening impossibility, the accused cannot be made a criminal.
23. The present criminal revision petitions are disposed off accordingly.
24. TCR be sent back with the copy of this order.
